stories.title: 🏞️ Amos 1
summaryBullets: The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. (1:1).
And he said: (1:2).
Thus says the Lord: (1:3).
So I will send a fire upon the house of Hazael, and it shall devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad. (1:4).

I will break the gate-bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitants from the Valley of Aven,and him who holds the scepter from Beth-eden; and the people of Syria shall go into exile to Kir,”says the Lord. (1:5).
Thus says the Lord: (1:6).
So I will send a fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it shall devour her strongholds. (1:7).
I will cut off the inhabitants from Ashdod, and him who holds the scepter from Ashkelon;I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish,”says the Lord God. (1:8).
Thus says the Lord: (1:9).
So I will send a fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it shall devour her strongholds.” (1:10).
Thus says the Lord: (1:11).
So I will send a fire upon Teman, and it shall devour the strongholds of Bozrah.” (1:12).
Thus says the Lord: (1:13).
So I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour her strongholds,with shouting on the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind; (1:14).
and their king shall go into exile, he and his princes together,”says the Lord. (1:15).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 14:23–29 — Jeroboam II’s reign (northern context).
Leviticus 25:35–43 — Care for the poor; prohibition of harsh oppression.
Numbers 6:1–8 — Nazarite vow basics.
Amos 9:7 — God’s rule over all nations (later in the book).

translationNotes.term: “For three transgressions… and for four” (repeated formula)
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה פִשְׁעֵי… וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָה (ʿal-sheloshah pishʿê… veʿal-arbaʿah) — Greek (LXX): ἐπὶ τρισὶ… καὶ ἐπὶ τεσσάρων — Aramaic: על תלת… ועל ארבע
translationNotes.note: A rhetorical ladder signaling a full, overflowing measure of guilt, not a literal count.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָזִיר (nazir) — Greek (LXX): ναζιραῖος — Aramaic: נזירא (nazira)
translationNotes.note: Person set apart by vow (abstaining from wine, hair uncut, no corpse defilement). Forcing them to drink wine violates their consecration (2:11–12).

translationNotes.term: Selling the righteous for silver / the needy for sandals
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צַדִּיק (tsaddiq, ‘innocent’) / אֶבְיוֹן (evyon, ‘needy’) — Greek (LXX): δίκαιος / πτωχός — Aramaic: זכאי / מסכן
translationNotes.note: Judicial corruption and debt-slavery: people treated like cheap property (2:6).

stories.keyTakeaway: The same Judge who roars over the nations also indicts Judah and Israel for violence, slave-trading, idolatry, sexual sin, and crushing the poor.

stories.title: 🏞️ Amos 2
summaryBullets: Thus says the Lord: (2:1).
So I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the strongholds of Kerioth,and Moab shall die amid uproar, amid shouting and the sound of the trumpet; (2:2).
I will cut off the ruler from its midst, and will kill all its princes with him,”says the Lord. (2:3).
Thus says the Lord: (2:4).
So I will send a fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the strongholds of Jerusalem.” (2:5).
Thus says the Lord: (2:6).
those who trample the head of the poor into the dust of the earth and turn aside the way of the afflicted;a man and his father go in to the same girl, so that my holy name is profaned; (2:7).
they lay themselves down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge,and in the house of their God they drink the wine of those who have been fined. (2:8).
“Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars and who was as strong as the oaks;I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath. (2:9).
Also it was I who brought you up out of the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite. (2:10).
And I raised up some of your sons for prophets, and some of your young men for Nazirites. Is it not indeed so, O people of Israel?”declares the Lord. (2:11).
“But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and commanded the prophets, saying, ‘You shall not prophesy.’ (2:12).
“Behold, I will press you down in your place, as a cart full of sheaves presses down. (2:13).
Flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not retain his strength, nor shall the mighty save his life; (2:14).
he who handles the bow shall not stand, and he who is swift of foot shall not save himself, nor shall he who rides the horse save his life; (2:15).
and he who is stout of heart among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day,”declares the Lord. (2:16).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 14:23–29 — Jeroboam II’s reign (northern context).
Leviticus 25:35–43 — Care for the poor; prohibition of harsh oppression.
Numbers 6:1–8 — Nazarite vow basics.
Amos 9:7 — God’s rule over all nations (later in the book).

translationNotes.term: “For three transgressions… and for four” (repeated formula)
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה פִשְׁעֵי… וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָה (ʿal-sheloshah pishʿê… veʿal-arbaʿah) — Greek (LXX): ἐπὶ τρισὶ… καὶ ἐπὶ τεσσάρων — Aramaic: על תלת… ועל ארבע
translationNotes.note: A rhetorical ladder signaling a full, overflowing measure of guilt, not a literal count.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָזִיר (nazir) — Greek (LXX): ναζιραῖος — Aramaic: נזירא (nazira)
translationNotes.note: Person set apart by vow (abstaining from wine, hair uncut, no corpse defilement). Forcing them to drink wine violates their consecration (2:11–12).

translationNotes.term: Selling the righteous for silver / the needy for sandals
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צַדִּיק (tsaddiq, ‘innocent’) / אֶבְיוֹן (evyon, ‘needy’) — Greek (LXX): δίκαιος / πτωχός — Aramaic: זכאי / מסכן
translationNotes.note: Judicial corruption and debt-slavery: people treated like cheap property (2:6).

stories.keyTakeaway: The same Judge who roars over the nations also indicts Judah and Israel for violence, slave-trading, idolatry, sexual sin, and crushing the poor.

stories.title: 📣 Amos 3
summaryBullets: Hear this word that the Lord has spoken against you, O people of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt: (3:1).
“You only have I known of all the families of the earth;therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities. (3:2).
“Do two walk together, unless they have agreed to meet? (3:3).
Does a lion roar in the forest, when he has no prey?Does a young lion cry out from his den, if he has taken nothing? (3:4).
Does a bird fall in a snare on the earth, when there is no trap for it?Does a snare spring up from the ground, when it has taken nothing? (3:5).
Is a trumpet blown in a city, and the people are not afraid?Does disaster come to a city, unless the Lord has done it? (3:6).
“For the Lord God does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets. (3:7).
The lion has roared; who will not fear?The Lord God has spoken; who can but prophesy?” (3:8).

Proclaim to the strongholds in Ashdod and to the strongholds in the land of Egypt,and say, “Assemble yourselves on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great tumults within her, and the oppressed in her midst.” (3:9).
“They do not know how to do right,” declares the Lord, “those who store up violence and robbery in their strongholds.” (3:10).
Therefore thus says the Lord God: (3:11).

Thus says the Lord: “As the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear, so shall the people of Israel who dwell in Samaria be rescued, with the corner of a couch and part of a bed. (3:12).
“Hear, and testify against the house of Jacob,” declares the Lord God, the God of hosts, (3:13).
“that on the day I punish Israel for his transgressions, I will punish the altars of Bethel,and the horns of the altar shall be cut off and fall to the ground. (3:14).
I will strike the winter house along with the summer house, and the houses of ivory shall perish,and the great houses shall come to an end,”declares the Lord. (3:15).
crossRefs: Exodus 19:5–6 — Chosen to be a treasured possession and holy nation.
1 Kings 12:28–33 — Bethel’s shrine established by Jeroboam I.
Psalm 118:27 — Horns of the altar (cultic feature).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קַרְנוֹת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (qarnot ha-mizbeaḥ) — Greek (LXX): κέρατα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου — Aramaic: קרני מדבחא
translationNotes.note: Projections at altar corners. Cutting them off signals the end of sanctuary security (3:14).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּתֵּי שֵׁן (battei shen) — Greek (LXX): οἶκοι ἐλεφαντίνων — Aramaic: בתי שנא
translationNotes.note: Palaces decorated with ivory (cf. 1 Kgs 22:39). Symbols of elite excess slated for ruin (3:15).

stories.keyTakeaway: Privilege brings accountability. God’s revealed word makes prophecy inevitable, and judgment will strike Israel’s religious and luxury centers.

stories.title: 🌾 Amos 4
summaryBullets: “Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, who are on the mountain of Samaria,who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to your husbands, ‘Bring, that we may drink!’ (4:1).
The Lord God has sworn by his holiness that, behold, the days are coming upon you,when they shall take you away with hooks, even the last of you with fishhooks. (4:2).
And you shall go out through the breaches, each one straight ahead; and you shall be cast out into Harmon,”declares the Lord. (4:3).
“Come to Bethel, and transgress; to Gilgal, and multiply transgression;bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days; (4:4).
offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and proclaim freewill offerings, publish them; for so you love to do, O people of Israel!”declares the Lord God. (4:5).
“I gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places,yet you did not return to me,”declares the Lord. (4:6).

“I also withheld the rain from you when there were yet three months to the harvest;I would send rain on one city, and send no rain on another city;one field would have rain, and the field on which it did not rain would wither; (4:7).
so two or three cities would wander to another city to drink water, and would not be satisfied;yet you did not return to me,”declares the Lord. (4:8).
“I struck you with blight and mildew; your many gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees the locust devoured;yet you did not return to me,”declares the Lord. (4:9).

“I sent among you a pestilence after the manner of Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword,and carried away your horses, and I made the stench of your camp go up into your nostrils;yet you did not return to me,”declares the Lord. (4:10).
“I overthrew some of you, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were as a brand plucked out of the burning;yet you did not return to me,”declares the Lord. (4:11).
“Therefore thus I will do to you, O Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel!” (4:12).

For behold, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his thought,who makes the morning darkness, and treads on the heights of the earth— the Lord, the God of hosts, is his name! (4:13).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 28:15–68 — Covenant curses echo in the disasters listed.
2 Kings 17:7–12 — Northern Israel’s sins and shrines.
Psalm 139:1–4 — God knows thoughts (divine knowledge).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פָּרוֹת הַבָּשָׁן (parot ha-Bashan) — Greek (LXX): δάμαλεις τοῦ Βασάν — Aramaic: תורתא דבשן
translationNotes.note: Bashan = rich pastureland. Metaphor for indulgent elites who crush the needy (4:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צִנּוֹת/סִירוֹת (tsinnôt/sîrôt) — Greek (LXX): ἄγκιστρα — Aramaic: צינין
translationNotes.note: Imagery aligns with Assyrian practice of leading captives with hooks (4:2).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֵּית־אֵל / גִּלְגָּל — Greek (LXX): Βαιθηλ / Γαλγαλ — Aramaic: בית אל / גלגל
translationNotes.note: Shrine sites. Pilgrimage and offerings there are condemned when paired with oppression (4:4–5).

stories.keyTakeaway: Religious activity without justice is empty. Repeated discipline failed to bring repentance—so judgment is coming from the Creator Himself.

stories.title: 🌌 Amos 5
summaryBullets: Hear this word that I take up over you in lamentation, O house of Israel: (5:1).
“Fallen, no more to rise, is the virgin Israel;forsaken on her land, with none to raise her up.” (5:2).
For thus says the Lord God: (5:3).
For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: (5:4).
but do not seek Bethel,and do not enter into Gilgal or cross over to Beersheba;for Gilgal shall surely go into exile, and Bethel shall come to nothing.” (5:5).
Seek the Lord and live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, with none to quench it for Bethel, (5:6).
O you who turn justice to wormwood and cast down righteousness to the earth! (5:7).

He who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns deep darkness into the morning and darkens the day into night,who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the surface of the earth,the Lord is his name; (5:8).
who makes destruction flash forth against the strong, so that destruction comes upon the fortress. (5:9).
They hate him who reproves in the gate, and they abhor him who speaks the truth. (5:10).

Therefore because you trample on the poor and you exact taxes of grain from him,you have built houses of hewn stone, but you shall not dwell in them;you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink their wine. (5:11).
For I know how many are your transgressions and how great are your sins—you who afflict the righteous, who take a bribe, and turn aside the needy in the gate. (5:12).
Therefore he who is prudent will keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time. (5:13).
Seek good, and not evil, that you may live;and so the Lord, the God of hosts, will be with you, as you have said. (5:14).
Hate evil, and love good, and establish justice in the gate;it may be that the Lord, the God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph. (5:15).
Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the Lord: (5:16).
and in all vineyards there shall be wailing, for I will pass through your midst,”says the Lord. (5:17).
Woe to you who desire the day of the Lord! Why would you have the day of the Lord?It is darkness, and not light, (5:18).
as if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him,or went into the house and leaned his hand against the wall, and a serpent bit him. (5:19).
Is not the day of the Lord darkness, and not light, and gloom with no brightness in it? (5:20).
“I hate, I despise your feasts, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies. (5:21).
Even though you offer me your burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them;and the peace offerings of your fattened animals, I will not look upon them. (5:22).
Take away from me the noise of your songs; to the melody of your harps I will not listen. (5:23).
But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream. (5:24).
“Did you bring to me sacrifices and offerings during the forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel? (5:25).
You shall take up Sikkuth your king, and Kiyyun your star-god—your images that you made for yourselves, (5:26).
and I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,” says the Lord, whose name is the God of hosts. (5:27).
crossRefs: Amos 4:4–5 — Empty worship already rebuked.
Job 9:9 — Pleiades and Orion named with God’s power in creation.
Isaiah 1:10–17 — God rejects sacrifices without justice.
Acts 7:42–43 — Stephen cites Amos 5 about carried idols.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִשְׁפָּט (mishpāṭ) / צְדָקָה (tsedāqāh) — Greek (LXX): κρίμα / δικαιοσύνη — Aramaic: דִּינָא / זִדְקָא
translationNotes.note: Legal rightness and relational fairness; Amos centers on these at the city gate (5:7) (5:15) (5:24).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יוֹם יְהוָה (yom YHWH) — Greek (LXX): ἡμέρα Κυρίου — Aramaic: יומא דיי
translationNotes.note: A decisive intervention by God. In Amos it brings judgment on presumptuous worshipers (5:18–20).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כִּימָה (Kimah) / כְּסִיל (Kesil) — Greek (LXX): Πλειάδες / Ὠρίων — Aramaic: כימה / כסיל
translationNotes.note: Named star clusters used to point to the Creator’s power (5:8).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַּׁעַר (shaʿar) — Greek (LXX): πύλη — Aramaic: תרעא
translationNotes.note: City gate = justice venue (elders sit, cases judged). Corruption here warps society (5:10) (5:12) (5:15).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סִכּוּת (Sikkuth) / כִּיּוּן (Kaiwan) — Greek (LXX, Acts 7): Ῥεμφάν — Aramaic: סכות / כיון
translationNotes.note: Probable astral deities/objects. LXX tradition reflected in Acts uses another name (Remphan).

stories.keyTakeaway: Real repentance seeks God and practices justice. The Day of the LORD is not automatic safety; ritual without righteousness brings darkness.

stories.title: 🏛️ Amos 6
summaryBullets: “Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria,the notable men of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes! (6:1).

Pass over to Calneh, and see, and from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines.Are you better than these kingdoms? Or is their territory greater than your territory, (6:2).
O you who put far away the day of disaster and bring near the seat of violence? (6:3).
“Woe to those who lie on beds of ivory and stretch themselves out on their couches,and eat lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall, (6:4).
who sing idle songs to the sound of the harp and like David invent for themselves instruments of music, (6:5).
who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph! (6:6).
Therefore they shall now be the first of those who go into exile, and the revelry of those who stretch themselves out shall pass away.” (6:7).
The Lord God has sworn by himself, declares the Lord, the God of hosts: (6:8).
And if ten men remain in one house, they shall die. (6:9).

And when one's relative, the one who anoints him for burial, shall take him up to bring the bones out of the house, and shall say to him who is in the innermost parts of the house, “Is there still anyone with you?” he shall say, “No”; and he shall say, “Silence! We must not mention the name of the Lord.” (6:10).
For behold, the Lord commands, and the great house shall be struck down into fragments, and the little house into bits. (6:11).
Do horses run on rocks? Does one plow there with oxen?But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood— (6:12).
you who rejoice in Lo-debar, who say, “Have we not by our own strength captured Karnaim for ourselves?” (6:13).
“For behold, I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel,” declares the Lord, the God of hosts;“and they shall oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.” (6:14).
crossRefs: 1 Kings 10:18–22 — Ivory, luxury in royal settings (symbol parallels).
Amos 5:7; Amos 5:24 — Justice turned to bitterness; call for justice to flow.
2 Kings 17:6 — Assyrian exile of the northern kingdom (historical outcome).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צִיּוֹן / שֹׁמְרוֹן — Greek (LXX): Σιών / Σαμάρεια — Aramaic: ציון / שמרון
translationNotes.note: Jerusalem (Judah) and Samaria (Israel) alike are targeted for complacency (6:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יוֹסֵף (Yosef) — Greek (LXX): Ἰωσήφ — Aramaic: יוסף
translationNotes.note: Shorthand for Israel/Ephraim in the north. Not grieving “Joseph” means ignoring the nation’s collapse (6:6).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא דְבָר (‘Lo-debar’) / קַרְנַיִם (Karnaim) — Greek (LXX): Λωδαβάρ / Καρναΐν — Aramaic: לא דבר / קרנין
translationNotes.note: Conquest boasts. The names underscore pride in military success that God overturns (6:13).

stories.keyTakeaway: Indulgent leaders ignore national collapse and pervert justice. Their comfort will flip to captivity, and their boasts to defeat.

stories.title: 📏 Amos 7
summaryBullets: This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, he was forming locusts when the latter growth was just beginning to sprout, and behold, it was the latter growth after the king's mowings. (7:1).
When they had finished eating the grass of the land, I said, (7:2).
The Lord relented concerning this: “It shall not be,” said the Lord. (7:3).
This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, the Lord God was calling for a judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was eating up the land. (7:4).
Then I said, (7:5).
The Lord relented concerning this: “This also shall not be,” said the Lord God. (7:6).
This is what he showed me: behold, the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand. (7:7).
And the Lord said to me, “Amos, what do you see?” And I said, “A plumb line.” Then the Lord said, (7:8).
the high places of Isaac shall be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.” (7:9).
Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words. (7:10).
For thus Amos has said, (7:11).
And Amaziah said to Amos, “O seer, go, flee away to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and prophesy there, (7:12).
but never again prophesy at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is a temple of the kingdom.” (7:13).
Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, “I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but I was a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs. (7:14).
But the Lord took me from following the flock, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’ (7:15).
Now therefore hear the word of the Lord. (7:16).
Therefore thus says the Lord: (7:17).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 14:23–29 — Jeroboam II’s reign in Israel (historical setting).
2 Kings 17:6 — Israel’s exile to Assyria (later outcome).
Jeremiah 1:11–12 — Wordplay vision and confirmation motif (vision → declaration).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֲנָךְ (ʾanakh, possibly ‘plumb line’/‘tin’) — Greek (LXX): ἀδόκιμος/ἄδοξος readings vary — Aramaic: אנך
translationNotes.note: Tool/metaphor for testing straightness. Here, God measures Israel and announces no further passing-over (7:7–9).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גִּזַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ (gizzat ha-melech) — Greek (LXX): κουρὰ βασιλέως — Aramaic: גזיתא דמלכא
translationNotes.note: The first cutting reserved for the king; the locusts hit what remained (7:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָבִיא… בֶּן־נָבִיא (navi… ben-navi) — Greek (LXX): προφήτης… υἱὸς προφήτου — Aramaic: נביא… בר נביא
translationNotes.note: “Son of a prophet” = member/trainee of a prophetic guild. Amos insists he was a herdsman until God sent him (7:14).

stories.keyTakeaway: Three visions show judgment measured and briefly withheld, then fixed by a plumb line. Resistance from Bethel’s priest brings a direct sentence: exile and personal ruin.

stories.title: 🧺 Amos 8
summaryBullets: This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, a basket of summer fruit. (8:1).
And he said, “Amos, what do you see?” And I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the Lord said to me, (8:2).
The songs of the temple shall become wailings in that day,”declares the Lord God.“So many dead bodies!”“They are thrown everywhere!”“Silence!” (8:3).
Hear this, you who trample on the needy and bring the poor of the land to an end, (8:4).

saying, “When will the new moon be over, that we may sell grain?And the Sabbath, that we may offer wheat for sale,that we may make the ephah small and the shekel great and deal deceitfully with false balances, (8:5).
that we may buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals and sell the chaff of the wheat?” (8:6).
The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob:“Surely I will never forget any of their deeds. (8:7).
Shall not the land tremble on this account, and everyone mourn who dwells in it,and all of it rise like the Nile, and be tossed about and sink again, like the Nile of Egypt?” (8:8).
“And on that day,” declares the Lord God, “I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight. (8:9).

I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation;I will bring sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head;I will make it like the mourning for an only son and the end of it like a bitter day. (8:10).
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the Lord God, “when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord. (8:11).
They shall wander from sea to sea, and from north to east;they shall run to and fro, to seek the word of the Lord, but they shall not find it. (8:12).
“In that day the lovely virgins and the young men shall faint for thirst. (8:13).
Those who swear by the Guilt of Samaria, and say, ‘As your god lives, O Dan,’and, ‘As the Way of Beersheba lives,’ they shall fall, and never rise again.” (8:14).
crossRefs: Leviticus 19:35–36 — Honest weights and measures commanded.
Amos 5:26–27 — Idols and coming exile (linked charges).
1 Samuel 3:1 — Rare visions/words in a prior period (scarcity of revelation).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קַיִץ (qayits, ‘summer fruit’) / קֵץ (qets, ‘end’) — Greek (LXX): θέρους / τέλος — Aramaic: קיץ / קץ
translationNotes.note: Sound-play ties the ripe basket to Israel’s imminent ‘end’ (8:1–2).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֹאזְנֵי מִרְמָה (moznei mirmah) — Greek (LXX): ζυγοὶ ἀδικίας — Aramaic: מאזני דשקרא
translationNotes.note: Cheating scales condemned along with mixing chaff/sweepings into grain (8:5).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רָעָב… לִשְׁמֹעַ אֵת דִּבְרֵי יְהוָה (raʿav… lishmoaʿ et divrei YHWH) — Greek (LXX): λιμὸς… τοῦ ἀκοῦσαι λόγον Κυρίου — Aramaic: כפן… למשמע פתגמי יי
translationNotes.note: Withheld revelation as judgment; people search everywhere and collapse without it (8:11–13).

stories.keyTakeaway: Judgment targets economic fraud and religious hypocrisy. The severest blow is silence—no word from God—so seekers stagger without guidance.

stories.title: 🛖 Amos 9
summaryBullets: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said: (9:1).
“If they dig into Sheol, from there shall my hand take them;if they climb up to heaven, from there I will bring them down. (9:2).

If they hide themselves on the top of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them;and if they hide from my sight at the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them. (9:3).
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it shall kill them;and I will fix my eyes upon them for evil and not for good.” (9:4).
The Lord God of hosts,he who touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn,and all of it rises like the Nile, and sinks again, like the Nile of Egypt; (9:5).
who builds his upper chambers in the heavens and founds his vault upon the earth;who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the surface of the earth—the Lord is his name. (9:6).
“Are you not like the Cushites to me, O people of Israel?” declares the Lord.“Did I not bring up Israel from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor and the Syrians from Kir? (9:7).

Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the surface of the ground, except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,”declares the Lord. (9:8).
“For behold, I will command, and shake the house of Israel among all the nationsas one shakes with a sieve, but no pebble shall fall to the earth. (9:9).
All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, who say, ‘Disaster shall not overtake or meet us.’ (9:10).
“In that day I will raise up the booth of David that is fallenand repair its breaches, and raise up its ruins and rebuild it as in the days of old, (9:11).
that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations who are called by my name,” declares the Lord who does this. (9:12).

“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the Lord, “when the plowman shall overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes him who sows the seed;the mountains shall drip sweet wine, and all the hills shall flow with it. (9:13).

I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel, and they shall rebuild the ruined cities and inhabit them;they shall plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they shall make gardens and eat their fruit. (9:14).
I will plant them on their land, and they shall never again be uprooted out of the land that I have given them,”says the Lord your God. (9:15).
crossRefs: Psalm 139:7–12 — No fleeing from God’s presence (inescapability theme).
Deuteronomy 30:1–5 — Return from exile and restoration to the land.
Acts 15:15–18 — James cites Amos 9:11–12 regarding the nations called by God’s name.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֻכַּת דָּוִד (sukkat David, ‘hut/booth’) — Greek (LXX): σκηνὴ Δαυίδ — Aramaic: סכּתא דדוד
translationNotes.note: Image of a collapsed royal shelter restored—dynastic/kingly house rebuilt (9:11).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew MT: שְׁאֵרִית אֱדוֹם (‘remnant of Edom’) — Greek (LXX): κατάλοιπα τῶν ἀνθρώπων (‘remnant of men’) — Aramaic: שירית אדום / שירית אנשא
translationNotes.note: Textual paths differ; Acts 15 follows the LXX, stressing “all nations” called by God’s name (9:12).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כַּפְתּוֹר (Kaphtor) / קִיר (Kir) — Greek (LXX): Καππαδοκία? (var. identifications) / Κίρ — Aramaic: כפדור / קיר
translationNotes.note: Origins/destinations in God’s movements of peoples: Philistines from Caphtor; Arameans to/from Kir (9:7).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל (Sheʾol) — Greek (LXX): ᾅδης (Hades) — Aramaic: שאולא (Sheʾola)
translationNotes.note: The realm of the dead; used in the “no escape” list (9:2).

stories.keyTakeaway: Judgment is inescapable, yet not total. After sifting, God restores David’s fallen shelter and brings overflowing harvest and secure planting.
